Pay and benefits, in plain language.

Every posting shows the rate before you apply. This page explains what sits behind that number, and what to ask before you sign.

Estimate my pay Search jobs

How a pay package is built

Four parts to look at

Hourly rate

The taxable base pay for each hour worked. It is the number on the posting.

Stipends

Some travel contracts include housing and meal stipends. Whether they apply depends on the contract and on your own circumstances.

Overtime and call

Overtime, on-call and callback terms differ by facility. They are listed before you accept.

Guaranteed hours

How many hours a week the contract guarantees, and what happens if a shift is cancelled.

Before you sign

Questions worth asking every time

A good recruiter answers these without being asked. Ours do, but here is the list anyway.

  • What is the hourly rate, and what is the weekly gross at my contracted hours?The estimate on the posting assumes the listed hours.
  • Are any stipends included, and what do I need to qualify for them?Tax treatment depends on your situation. Ask a tax professional about yours.
  • How many hours are guaranteed?And what is the policy if the facility cancels a shift.
  • What are the overtime, holiday and call rates?Get them in writing in the contract.
  • What happens if the contract ends early?The terms should be spelled out for both sides.

What we always do

  • Show the rate on the posting, before you apply
  • Walk through the full package before you accept
  • Put every term in the contract, in plain language
  • Answer pay questions within one business day
